subject: Clarifying PayFlux encryption controls and BYOK options
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@payflux.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: payments+sec@payflux.com

Subject: Quick follow-up on encryption & residency items from today's demo

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo this morning — it was helpful. We have a couple of specific items the security and platform teams want clarified before we move to an internal risk review:

- In-transit encryption: do you support TLS 1.3 only or fall back to TLS 1.2 for older clients? Any details on cipher suites?
- At-rest encryption: is server-side encryption AES-256 standard?
- BYOK: PayFlux prefers customer-managed keys. Can Redwood integrate with AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault for key wrapping, and do you support HSM-backed keys (BYOHSM) for FIPS boundary requirements?
- Key custody model: can keys be rotated by PayFlux on-demand and still be compatible with snapshots/backups?
- Logging and retention: we need to demonstrate that PII is not logged in plaintext and have retention SLAs (30/90/365 options). Can you provide your logging sampling/PII redaction approach?
- Residency: single-region EU option is a hard requirement for one of our product lines — what's the process and timeline to provision a private deployment in eu-west-1?

If you can send a short matrix (one page) mapping these items to the supported options and any blocking caveats, that would be perfect. Also copying legal: legal@payflux.com for any procurement/contract flags.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Security — PayFlux

--
Lena Ortiz

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on encryption & residency items from today's demo

Hi Lena — really appreciate the clear list. I pulled together a concise matrix and a recommended POA for a PayFlux POC (attached). High level answers below; the attached PDF has the full matrix and caveats.

- In-transit: Redwood enforces TLS 1.3 for hosted endpoints by default. We can enable TLS 1.2 for specific legacy clients during a migration window; cipher suites follow AWS recommendations (AES-GCM, ECDHE). We will include explicit cipher lists in the matrix.
- At-rest: yes — server-side AES-256 (GCM) is standard for hosted and dedicated. For Private deployments we also support disk-level encryption per-customer.
- BYOK: We support KMS integration patterns for AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault (key wrapping + envelope encryption). HSM-backed keys are supported via customer KMS that exposes an API (e.g., AWS CloudHSM behind AWS KMS). Full BYOHSM (where Redwood manages an HSM for you) is treated as a Private offering and requires a separate SLA.
- Key rotation: customer-initiated rotations are supported. For hosted models we use an envelope key approach so object re-wrap is handled online without needing full re-encryption. Snapshot compatibility is documented in the matrix — short answer: yes, rotations are compatible; we keep a short grace period to allow rolling rewraps.
- Logging / PII: Redwood doesn't log unredacted request bodies by default. We provide structured telemetry: token counts, latency, model id, route; request/response payloads are stored only when customer enables debug logging. We can enable field-level redaction and masking for PII fields at ingestion. Retention windows 30/90/365 are configurable on Dedicated/Private; hosted defaults to 90 days.
- Residency: Private deployments in eu-west-1 are on our roadmap and possible via Private (VPC) provisioning. Typical lead time is 6-8 weeks for initial setup + onboarding; Dedicated reserved capacity in-region can often be faster (3-4 weeks) depending on capacity.

Next steps I propose:
1) See attached one-pager matrix (redwood-encryption-matrix.pdf).
2) If that looks OK, we schedule a 30-minute tech sync next week with Neha (security) and Monica (onboarding) to lock the integration pattern.
3) We'll produce a short MMAP (minimal migration and acceptance plan) for the PayFlux POC — I attached a starter spreadsheet (payflux-poc-mmap.xlsx).

Would Wednesday 2026-10-28 10:00am PT work for the tech sync?

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Lena / team — adding a few technical clarifications so legal/architects have the specifics for their risk review.

- TLS: We require TLS 1.3 for client connections; if PayFlux has legacy clients we can negotiate a TLS 1.2 compatibility window but it will be limited and logged for deprecation. Cipher suites: we support ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and CHACHA20_POLY1305 for mobile clients; full list is in the matrix.
- BYOK/HSM: The integration patterns are:
  * Bring-your-own-key (customer KMS): Redwood uses envelope encryption. Customer KMS holds the root key; Redwood stores only wrapped keys. Rotation is a KMS operation; we support re-wrap workflows.
  * BYOHSM (Private): Customer provides HSM-backed keys and we run the private control plane in your VPC. This satisfies FIPS 140-2/3 boundary requirements; proof points and HSM attestation reports are part of the security package.
- HSM certifications: If PayFlux requires FIPS-level attestation, we will provide HSM vendor attestation and control plane diagrams. Running in Private mode avoids having Redwood ever see unwrapped key material.
- PII redaction: Our ingestion pipeline has a configurable pre-processing layer that can apply regex and ML-based entity detection to redact or tokenise PII before it reaches the model runtime. We can provide sample redaction configs for common payment PII (card numbers, SSNs).
- Audit logs: We can deliver an audit bundle (access logs, key rotation logs, admin actions) with configurable retention. For Dedicated/Private we can set retention policy to 30/90/365 as requested and export logs to an external SIEM (S3/Blob) for PayFlux retention policies.

I'll join the technical sync and bring a short checklist that the security team can use for an internal go/no-go.

-Neha
